title: が好き ／ 嫌い ／ 上手 ／ 下手
meaning: The object of liking, disliking and skill is marked with が.
simpleExplanation: To say you like, dislike, are good at or bad at something, the thing is marked with が: 音楽が好きです "I like music". In English "like" is a verb with an object, but in Japanese 好き is a な-adjective, so the thing you like is the subject ("music is likeable to me"). The same goes for 嫌い (dislike), 上手 (good at) and 下手 (bad at). To like doing something, add の to the verb: 泳ぐのが好きです.
whenUsed: Talking about tastes (food, music, sports), hobbies, and skills. 上手 is used for other people's skills; for your own use 得意 or simply say what you can do.
formation: Noun + が + 好きです／嫌いです／上手です／下手です

examples.ja: 私は日本の音楽が好きです。
examples.reading: わたしは にほんの おんがくが すきです。
examples.note: Thing liked + が + 好きです.

examples.reading: おとうとは やさいが きらいです。
examples.note: Thing disliked + が + 嫌いです.

examples.ja: 田中さんは料理が上手です。
examples.reading: たなかさんは りょうりが じょうずです。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka is good at cooking.
examples.note: Skill + が + 上手です (about someone else).

examples.ja: 私は泳ぐのが好きです。
examples.reading: わたしは およぐのが すきです。
examples.note: Verb + の turns the action into a noun so が can follow.

examples.reading: わたしは うたが へたです。
examples.note: Being modest about yourself with 下手 is natural.

similarGrammar.difference: Same が for the object of a feeling word.
Also take が for their object.
好き, 嫌い, 上手, 下手 are all な-adjectives: 好きな, 好きじゃない.

commonMistakes.why: 好き is not a verb; its object takes が.
好き is a な-adjective despite ending in き.
A verb needs の before が to become a noun.

usageNotes: All four are な-adjectives: 好きな人, 好きじゃない. 大好き = love, 大嫌い = hate. Saying 上手 about your own skill sounds boastful; use 得意（とくい）instead. To say "like doing X", nominalise: 泳ぐのが好きです.
jlptTips: If the word after the blank is 好き・嫌い・上手・下手, the particle is が.
If a verb comes before 好き, the blank is のが (verb + の + が).
